elements.element: No non-compete restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Ono and its Affiliates remain prohibited from Commercializing or licensing any defined “Competing Product” in the Ono Territory during the first twelve months of the term.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause restricts Ono’s activities with respect to products containing agents within two specified pharmaceutical categories, which is a product/field-of-use restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: “Competing Product” covers any product containing an agent within either of two broadly defined classes. Binimetinib and Encorafenib are named only as exclusions, not as the sole competing product subject to the restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies only “[d]uring the first twelve (12) months of the term,” and the original post-termination restriction has been removed.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer lasts no more than twelve months.
elements.evidence: The operative restriction is expressly limited to the first twelve months of the agreement term.

elements.element: The restriction carves out Customer’s internal development activities.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the restriction does not apply to Ono’s or its Affiliates’ internal Development activities.

elements.element: The restriction carves out competing products obtained through acquisitions.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes any Competing Product acquired by Ono or its Affiliates through a merger, acquisition, or similar transaction.

result.reason: The redline removes the post-termination tail, caps the covenant at twelve months, and adds the required internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. It nevertheless retains a non-compete covering broad product classes rather than a specifically named competing product, so neither position is fully satisfied. It also narrows Array’s restriction to twelve months even though the rule concerns restrictions on Customer, thereby changing an unrelated reciprocal commercial obligation. Drafting is generally intelligible but retains the grammatical error “neither Ono or,” broad defined-product coverage, and an unresolved redacted period in the separate Array-commercialization provision.
